recognize_zh: 箭頭所指的紅血球中央有一塊血紅素染色的圓點，外圍一圈淡色環，再外面又是一圈粉紅邊緣，形成「靶心」外觀，即標靶細胞（target cell, codocyte）。
features: Red cells with a central dense hemoglobinized spot surrounded by a pale ring and a peripheral rim of hemoglobin (bull's-eye pattern)
Target cells are normal to slightly large in size and constitute a substantial proportion of the field
Admixed normocytic red cells with preserved or lost central pallor; a few folded cells showing linear pallor/drying artifact
No spherocytes, sickle cells, or red cell inclusions evident
Scattered small platelets in the background; low cell density area of the smear
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear viewed at high power in a thin area shows numerous target cells (codocytes), characterized by a central hemoglobinized zone, a surrounding pale annulus and a peripheral rim of hemoglobin (arrows). The remaining red cells are largely normocytic; a few show folding or linear pallor consistent with slide preparation artifact. No sickle cells, spherocytes, basophilic stippling or inclusions are identified in this field, and platelets appear adequate on this limited view. Findings are consistent with target cell formation; correlation with hemoglobin electrophoresis and liver function is recommended to distinguish hemoglobinopathy, thalassemia and liver disease.

ddx.vs: Stomatocytes have a slit-like or mouth-shaped central pallor rather than a central hemoglobin dot within a pale ring.
Artifactual targets are confined to thick areas or one field and often show refractile, irregular pallor, whereas true target cells are evenly distributed in the monolayer.
HbC and HbSC disease show intraerythrocytic rhomboid or 'Washington monument' crystals and folded cells in addition to targets, which are not seen here.
